title: Technology Sector Update for 01/02/2018: MICT,CISQ,IMPV,BABA,GOOG,GOOGL
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT +0.53%
AAPL +1.77%
IBM +0.65%
CSCO +1.48%
GOOG +1.88%
Technology stocks still were firming Tuesday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding over 1.1% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 1.6% gain.
In industry news:
Alibaba Group Holding ( BABA ) rose over 6% on Tuesday, topping out at $183.13 a share, following reports its UC browser is quickly becoming a viable challenger to Google's (GOOG,GOOGL) Chrome market dominance. The browser already is becoming the application of choice for hundreds of millions of consumers in developing markets, according to a Daily Mail report. The free app for Android devices is said to work better on less-expensive smartphone and in areas with intermittent coverage, the newspaper said.
Among technology stocks moving on news today:
Micronet Enertec Technologies ( MICT ) shares sprang over 56% to a new 52-week high of $1.75 a share on Tuesday after the aerospace and defense contractor said it has agreed to sell its Enertec Systems subsidiary to DPW Holdings ( DPW ) for $5.25 mln in cash at closing. DPW, through its Coolisys Technologies unit, will also assume about $4 mln in Enertec bank debt. Micronet said the deal supports its strategy of focusing on the rapidly growing mobile resource management space, while fortifying its balance sheet and significantly reducing debt. "We believe our improved cash position will enable us to expand our MRM offerings," Micronet CEO David Lucatz said in prepared remarks.
In other sector news:
+ Imperva ( IMPV ) advanced today after naming former Gigamon finance executive Mike Burns to its vacant CFO post. Former Imperva chief financial officer Terry Schmid left the company in October to pursue other interests.
+ Canadian Solar ( CSIQ ) rose Tuesday after the photovoltaic-panels company secured a $42.8 mln (AUD55.0 mln) facility commitment for the Oakey 2 solar farm in Queensland, Australia. The company also won the engineering, procurement and construction contract to complete work at the 70-megawatt facility as well as an operations and maintenance contract for the first two years following completion, expected in November.
